C-EXT-GALLERY-STATE.Summary: Make the extension gallery tell the truth about extension state: re-discovery preserves the enabled flag it already holds (a manifest whose incoming requests grew resets to the #298 re-approval path instead of silently keeping or silently dropping the flag), duplicate enable/disable toggles become honest backend no-ops that neither re-fence in-flight credentials nor re-enter the revocation machinery, discovery probes the scanned manifests concurrently under a named bound while scan read/parse failures surface beside the list as a distinct localized gallery notice in all ten locales, and the checkbox renders the newest fetched list generation so a late stale snapshot can never flip a toggle back.
C-EXT-GALLERY-STATE.Problem: Verified against the current worktree (branch spec/ext-gallery-state, base b702a7fe, which already contains C-EXT-EDIT-PROOF #321 and C-EXT-TRUST-COHERENCE #326); the wave-2 scout findings 4, 13, 14, 15 and 16 share one cause — the gallery treats the last list it received as the truth about extension state, and the backend feeds it lists that lie. (1) Re-discovery wipes the enabled flag: registry.register unconditionally builds the new state with enabled: false and overwrites any previous entry with the same id ("Overwrites any previous entry with the same id (re-discovery replaces stale state)", registry.rs:89-110, the literal at 97-102); mt_ext_discover registers every discovered manifest under the stream gate (mod.rs:85-101) and the gallery Refresh is the user-facing entry (index.vue:173-187) — so every Refresh silently disarms every enabled extension. (2) The toggle is UI-only protected: the checkbox's :disabled="toggling[ext.id]" (index.vue:45) is the only guard against a double toggle, while the backend commands are unconditional flag writes that bump the authorization_epoch every time they run (registry.rs:113-150) with no already-in-state short-circuit — a duplicate enable re-fences in-flight credentials and re-enters the mint/coverage path, a duplicate disable re-enters the revocation machinery (mod.rs:183-274), and both commands sit in the public allowlist (m001_validate.rs:98-104) so any caller can churn them. (3) Discovery is sequential: discover_extensions awaits probe_health one manifest at a time (discovery.rs:184-198), each probe a GET with a 5-second timeout (discovery.rs:142), so a Refresh over N extensions blocks for up to N×5 seconds. (4) Scan failures are swallowed: BLOCK_SCAN_READ_FAILED and BLOCK_SCAN_PARSE_FAILED log-and-continue (discovery.rs:93-118), discover_extensions returns a bare Vec with no failure channel, mt_ext_discover answers the plain list (mod.rs:85-101), and the gallery clears its error surface on every successful list fetch (index.vue:159, pinned by index.test.js:89-97) — a directory of broken manifests renders as a quiet empty gallery. (5) A stale list flips the toggle: the checkbox is a pure function of the last list (:checked="ext.enabled", index.vue:44), every toggle ends in an unconditional awaited refetch (index.vue:229), and fetchExtensions writes whatever list resolves last (index.vue:150-167) — an older in-flight mt_ext_list resolving after the refetch overwrites the newer truth with no outcome comparison. C-EXT-TRUST-COHERENCE (#326) already made the toggle ACTION outcome-aware for the failed-disable case (the revokePendingIds set at index.vue:140, the action choice at index.vue:197) — this change composes with that state and does not duplicate it; the display side stayed list-driven.
C-EXT-GALLERY-STATE.Relationship: Lineage, all landed: C-SEC-EXT-GRANT-BOUND (#298) owns the stored pairing grant, the enable coverage gate and the authorization_epoch semantics — this change preserves enabled only when the incoming manifest does not grow past what the stored manifest requested, so a preserved flag can never stand in for an approval that never happened: growth resets the flag and the next enable passes through the coverage gate (mod.rs:140-174) into ext_enable_reapproval_required when the grant does not cover the grown set, and the routes stay grant-bound regardless, so no path here confers new incoming rights. C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH owns the stream-gate discipline and the epoch fencing — register keeps bumping the authorization_epoch on every registration (the invalidation wording at registry.rs:197-203 stays true), the discover register loop stays inside its existing stream_gate block (mod.rs:91), and the new no-op toggle decisions read credentials strictly before any gate is taken, the mt_ext_enable pre-gate marker/secret-read precedent (mod.rs:121-138). C-SEC-AUDIT-FIXES T-005 owns the probe hygiene (loopback-only, no-proxy, no-redirect) — every probe keeps it byte-for-byte. C-STABILIZE owns the scan-directory canon — untouched. C-EXT-EDIT-PROOF (#321, approved) owns the edit pipeline and is untouched; its non-goals explicitly deferred this bundle. C-EXT-TRUST-COHERENCE (#326, approved) owns the revoke-pending marker, the retry-Disable action choice and the disable fence — composed, not reworked: the no-op disable checks the marker BEFORE short-circuiting, so a standing marker always sends the full revocation retry exactly as #326 pinned, the strict-absence success condition is unchanged, and the gallery retry set, its ten-locale texts (extensions.disableFailed, extensions.revokePending, en.json:1848-1851) and the re-approval mapping of #298 (index.vue:207-212) keep their meaning; the repository ten-locale canon (C-10/C-12/C-32/C-56 precedent) applies to the one new gallery string here. This bundle is one of four triaged from the 2026-11-22 wave-2 scout (B3 GALLERY-STATE; B1 EDIT-PROOF and B2 TRUST-COHERENCE are landed neighbors, B4 DELIVERY-HONESTY is an explicit non-goal here) and closes the interface half of the wave-2 acceptance criterion: the toggle reflects the real state, and a discovery refusal is visible.

Goals.Goal: Re-discovery stops wiping the enabled flag. registry.register consults the entry already stored under the same id and preserves its enabled flag whenever the incoming manifest requests no incoming capability that the stored manifest did not already request — the comparison runs over the incoming capability vocabulary of live_server::incoming_capability_names (live_server.rs:897), the same set the #298 enable coverage gate consults. A first registration for a fresh id keeps enabled: false exactly as today, and the stored manifest and the fresh health result always update. Every registration continues to bump the authorization_epoch: an in-flight credential that crosses a re-discovery is fenced exactly as today, and register's participation in the invalidation semantics of C-SEC-STREAM-AUTH/#298 is unchanged. The one moved pin is registry_re_register_overwrites (tests.rs:358-369), whose reset assertion moves to preservation while its single-entry overwrite and healthy-update assertions keep their meaning.

Manifest growth cannot ride a preserved flag. When the re-discovered manifest requests an incoming capability the previously stored manifest did not, register resets enabled to false with a distinct logged state, so the owner's next enable passes through the #298 coverage gate and refuses into ext_enable_reapproval_required when the stored pairing grant does not cover the grown set — the gallery already surfaces that instruction (index.vue:207-212). Shrinking or equal incoming sets preserve the flag, and non-incoming capability changes never affect the decision. This restores the invariant the coverage gate assumes: an enabled extension's manifest was covered by its stored grant at the last enable.

Duplicate toggles become honest backend no-ops. mt_ext_enable returns Ok without minting, without the coverage gate, without taking stream_gate and without an epoch bump when the registry already reports the extension enabled — after the #326 revoke-pending marker gate, which keeps running first exactly as today (mod.rs:121-131). mt_ext_disable takes its no-op decision before the fence from reads that hold neither gate nor session lock: with the marker read absent (Ok(false)), the secret verifiably absent through the strict read (auth::verify_secret_absent — an unreadable persistent store can never mean absent) and the registry already reporting the extension disabled, it returns Ok — no gate, no revocation retry, no epoch bump, no context drain replay; any marker error, a standing marker, a surviving secret or an enabled or unregistered id sends the full disable path exactly as today. The #326 recovery is therefore intact: a standing marker means the retry-disable runs the real revocation (the ext_disable_revoke_failed and clear-on-proof semantics unchanged), and the BLOCK_DISABLE_REVOKE_PENDING_UNRECORDED residual (a surviving secret with no marker) always re-enters the full path. The double-disable success leg of disable_revokes_and_verifies_absence (tests.rs:1824-1825) keeps passing — now by explicit no-op instead of harness luck — and a duplicate toggle no longer fences in-flight credentials, because the no-op paths bump no epoch.

Discovery probes concurrently within a named bound. discover_extensions probes the scanned manifests concurrently under a bounded named concurrency cap using the existing tokio runtime facilities (Semaphore/JoinSet are inside the current tokio features — no new dependency), each probe keeping its hygiene byte-for-byte (loopback-only, no-proxy, no-redirect, the 5-second per-probe timeout, discovery.rs:130-179) and the results keeping the manifests' scan order; the worst-case Refresh wait drops from N×5 seconds to roughly ceil(N/cap)×5 seconds, and health semantics are unchanged (true only on a success status). No progress channel and no cancellation are added — the gallery's existing loading state covers the wait.

Discovery reports what it could not read. discover_extensions returns the discovered extensions beside the scan failures — each failure carrying the path and a machine kind distinguishing read failures from parse failures — while the existing BLOCK_ logs stay; mt_ext_discover returns that outcome as its Ok payload (the command name, its allowlist entry at m001_validate.rs:98 and its registration are unchanged, and the sole production consumer is the gallery). The gallery renders a distinct localized scan-failure notice when the payload carries failures, in one new extensions-namespace key added to all ten static/locales files per the C-10/C-12/C-32/C-56 canon; the notice survives the awaited list fetch that follows discovery — a successful list must not clear it, which is precisely today's swallow at index.vue:159 — and is replaced only by the next discovery's outcome. Valid manifests keep registering and rendering exactly as today, including their preserved enabled state.

The checkbox stops trusting arrival order. Every list fetch carries a fetch generation; a resolved list lands only when its generation is still the newest, so an older snapshot resolving late never overwrites a newer one. The post-toggle refetch stays the awaited observation of record — there is no optimistic flip: the checkbox moves only on backend truth, the in-flight flag keeps disabling the input, and the refusal surfaces keep their semantics. The composed state machine is pinned: #326's revokePendingIds keeps governing the ACTION, #298's re-approval mapping keeps governing the enable refusal text, and the fetch-generation rule keeps the DISPLAY honest and the recovery state intact — a list discarded by the generation rule mutates neither the displayed list nor the revoke-pending id set (the cleanup runs only for the winning generation; named pin stale_fetch_discarded_by_generation_does_not_clear_revoke_pending); none of the three duplicates another.

Constraints.Constraint: Exact ObservedWriteScope, enumerated by reading the current tree:

Read-only anchors: auth.rs (get_revoke_pending, verify_secret_absent and the strict-absence discipline consumed through existing signatures — no new credential records and no marker semantics change); live_server.rs (incoming_capability_names consumed as-is; the data routes, the #326/#321 fence and ack work, pairing and stream handling untouched); src-tauri/src/main.rs (the command registration literal unchanged); m001_validate.rs (allowlist names unchanged); manifest.rs (parse_manifest consumed as-is); text_ops.rs, invoke.rs, live_bridge.rs (B1/B4 territory); editor.vue, textOps.js and textOps.test.js untouched; tests/renderer/components/extensionGallery.test.js untouched — its bare-undefined discover mock keeps passing because the component reads the new payload tolerantly (an absent failure field means no notice), so that suite moves no pin.

Lock and discipline: the preservation decision is computed inside the registry's existing lock discipline with no new lock; the discover register loop stays inside its existing stream_gate block (mod.rs:91); the no-op toggle decisions perform their marker/secret reads strictly before any gate is taken (the mt_ext_enable pre-gate precedent) and hold no gate across keyring I/O; the lock order stream_gate, then session, then leaf maps is unchanged.

Refusal codes and predecessor semantics are unchanged: ext_enable_revoke_pending, ext_disable_revoke_failed and ext_enable_reapproval_required keep their meanings and their gallery mappings; the #326 legs keep exact behavior (marker gate first on enable; marker standing or secret surviving sends the full disable path; the strict-absence success condition and its BLOCK_ log names unchanged); the new no-op states get distinct BLOCK_ logs in the files' existing voice; the epoch bump on every registration, enable and disable of the full paths is unchanged — only the no-op paths skip it, by definition of being no-ops.

Discovery honesty: per-probe hygiene byte-for-byte (loopback-only, no-proxy, no-redirect, 5-second timeout); the concurrency cap is a named bounded constant; result order follows scan order; health semantics unchanged; the payload shape extends in place with no new IPC channel, command name or allowlist change; the scan-failure entries carry machine kinds (read/parse) plus the path, with raw error text staying in the BLOCK_ logs.

Gallery honesty: no optimistic flip — the checkbox renders backend truth only; the scan-failure notice is a single additive surface below the list (the gallery stays a list plus toggle plus error/notice surfaces — no redesign, no per-card badges, no native dialog); exactly one new user-facing string, localized in all ten static/locales/*.json files under the extensions namespace (the extensions.disableFailed precedent at en.json:1848-1851); the existing keys keep their meaning.

Predecessor suites keep meaning with exactly one moved pin, named: registry_re_register_overwrites (tests.rs:358-369) moves its enabled-reset assertion to preservation. Everything else keeps passing unchanged: the registry idempotency pins (tests.rs:496-515), disable_revokes_and_verifies_absence including its double-disable success leg (tests.rs:1810-1826), disable_surfaces_revoke_failure and disable_refuses_unverified_revocation (tests.rs:1828-1857), the #326 gallery retry and mapping pins (index.test.js:167-238), the re-approval mapping pin (index.test.js:152-165), the refresh pins including the IPC-failure error-clear (index.test.js:70-120 — the discover IPC-rejection path is unchanged), the #298 grant/rebind suite, the #321 suites, the manifest URL hygiene pins and the sibling extensionGallery.test.js.

Repository artifacts stay English and the GRACE surface is synchronized (module contracts and CHANGE_SUMMARY entries of registry.rs, discovery.rs, mod.rs, tests.rs and index.vue; module maps; graph; verification); no version change, release, publication or deploy is authorized by this specification.

NonGoals.NonGoal: No delivery-honesty work (scout keys 18, 20, 10 — bundle B4): no endpoint publication retry, no doc_open ack channel, no InvokeError body sanitization.
No edit-pipeline work (scout keys 1, 2, 3, 11, 17, 19 — bundle B1, C-EXT-EDIT-PROOF #321): no ack channel, no dead-route or idempotency rework, no invoke retry or Retry-After change.
No trust-coherence work (scout keys 5, 7, 8, 12 — bundle B2, C-EXT-TRUST-COHERENCE #326): no marker semantic change, no new fence, no revoke/rebind rework — composition only, per the Goals.

No persistence: the registry and the enabled flag stay process-local; no restart migration — an extension enabled before a restart starts disabled exactly as today, and the first discovery after a restart registers fresh ids disabled.

No discovery redesign beyond the bound: no progress channel, no in-flight cancellation, no probe protocol, manifest-schema or directory-layout change; the unregistered-id enable behavior (mint-then-not-found) stays exactly as today.

No toggle redesign: no request-id dedup protocol on the toggle commands (a state check suffices for owner-initiated toggles), no change to the allowlist, command signatures or the checkbox interaction pattern.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Failing-first preservation: registry_re_register_preserves_enabled (the moved registry_re_register_overwrites pin) — enable a registered extension, re-register the same id with an equal-incoming-set manifest and fresh health: the entry stays enabled, the stored manifest and healthy values update, the map keeps exactly one entry; today the same sequence yields enabled:false (tests.rs:358-369 pins the reset), so the new assertions are red before the fix; the fresh-id leg (a first registration stays disabled) and the single-entry overwrite stay asserted.

Boundary and fencing insurance committed with the family: registry_re_register_growth_resets_enabled — a re-discovered manifest requesting an incoming name the stored manifest lacked resets enabled to false with the distinct logged state (guarding against an unconditional-preserve implementation; behaviorally green both before and after, and its composed leg — growth reset, then mt_ext_enable with a stored grant not covering the grown name — refuses with ext_enable_reapproval_required exactly as the #298 pin grow_after_pairing_enable_is_refused_to_reapproval at tests.rs:2353-2371 already does for the enable path; approved_rebind_captures_the_presented_declared_set (tests.rs:2452-2506) stays green under preservation deliberately — its :2482 narrowing re-registration rides an enabled record and asserts nothing about the flag afterwards); registry_re_register_still_bumps_authorization_epoch — a preserved-enabled re-registration changes the authorization_epoch and authorization_epoch still answers for the enabled id (green today, insurance after).

Failing-first no-op toggles: a second mt_ext_enable on an already-enabled extension answers Ok with the authorization_epoch unchanged and no mint (today registry.enable runs unconditionally and bumps the epoch at registry.rs:113-130, so the epoch-equality assertion is red before the fix); a second mt_ext_disable on an extension whose marker reads absent and whose secret verifiably is absent answers Ok with the epoch unchanged (today the full path bumps via registry.disable and re-enters revocation — red); and the same family keeps the predecessor legs green: a standing marker sends the full retry-disable (ext_disable_revoke_failed on the fail_delete pattern, clear on success), an unreadable persistent store sends the full path (the disable_refuses_unverified_revocation modes keep their refusals), the #326 clear-on-proof pins keep passing, an unregistered id keeps the not-found refusal, and the double-disable success leg of disable_revokes_and_verifies_absence (tests.rs:1824-1825) keeps passing.

Failing-first bounded concurrency: over the parameterized discovery variant (scan dirs and prober injectable — internal test plumbing following the extension_dirs_for_profile precedent at discovery.rs:50-67, the env-driven production entry keeping its behavior), a counting fake prober over several manifests observes a maximum concurrency of at least two and never above the named cap, with results in scan order (today the sequential loop at discovery.rs:188-195 observes exactly one — red before the fix); the production env entry keeps its signature and behavior.

Failing-first scan surfacing: the discovery outcome carries the scan failures beside the extensions — in a fixture directory an unreadable entry (a directory named with a .json extension) and an unparseable entry (invalid JSON) each yield a failure naming the path and the machine kind, while the valid manifest still lands in the extensions list, and mt_ext_discover's Ok payload carries both lists (today there is no failure channel — the baseline red is the missing shape, the C-STREAM-BUDGET compile-error red precedent); the BLOCK_ logs stay in place.

Failing-first gallery notice: a refresh whose discover payload carries scan failures renders the distinct localized notice and the notice SURVIVES the successful list fetch that follows (today the discover payload is ignored and a successful list clears the error surface at index.vue:159 — red), while the next failure-free refresh replaces the notice with nothing; the existing refresh pins (index.test.js:70-120, including the discover IPC-failure error-clear at 89-97) keep passing unchanged, and the new extensions-namespace key exists in every one of the ten static/locales/*.json files.

Failing-first stale list: two in-flight mt_ext_list fetches where an older generation resolves after a newer one render the NEWER list's cards (today the last resolution wins in fetchExtensions, index.vue:150-167 — red); the composition legs stay green in the same family: the post-toggle refetch is awaited and its list renders, and the #326 retry pins (index.test.js:167-238) plus the revoke-pending mapping pin (index.test.js:224-238) pass unchanged.

Predecessor suites: every suite named in Constraints passes after the fix with unchanged assertions, with the single moved pin of the first criterion named in the plan; graph ownership, module maps and the file-local contracts (MODULE_CONTRACT, MODULE_MAP, CHANGE_SUMMARY) of registry.rs, discovery.rs, mod.rs, tests.rs and index.vue describe the final implementation, with the preservation, growth-reset, no-op and scan-failure semantics documented where they live.

VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: Each named failing-first family — the re-register preservation (red against the tests.rs:358-369 reset pin), the no-op toggles (red against the unconditional epoch bumps), the bounded probe concurrency (red against the sequential loop), the scan-failure payload and its gallery notice (red against the swallowed-and-cleared behavior), and the stale-list generation rule (red against last-resolve-wins) — fails before the fix and passes after it; the boundary-insurance pins (growth reset, epoch-continues-to-bump) are committed with the family and green in both runs; every predecessor suite named in Constraints passes with unchanged assertions and the one moved pin is named in the plan; the sibling extensionGallery.test.js stays green without edits. Before archiving: grace lint --path . --change C-EXT-GALLERY-STATE --assertions final --run-commands, then grace lint --path . --assertions current and grace status --path . --with modules --json.

Assumptions.Assumption: The payload field names of the discovery outcome (the extensions list and the failed-manifest entries with their machine kinds), the concurrency cap value, the notice element/class in index.vue, the new locale key name and the no-op BLOCK_ log names are plan-level constants within the bounds pinned here; the wire shape keeps the component tolerant of an absent failure field so the sibling suite's undefined mock stays valid.

The parameterized discovery variant (dirs and prober seams) is internal test plumbing on the extension_dirs_for_profile precedent; production behavior is unchanged and still enters through the env-driven wrapper.

AffectedAreas stays M-045-only, following the C-SEC-EXT-GRANT-BOUND and C-EXT-TRUST-COHERENCE precedent (extensionGallery/index.vue in scope, M-011 not claimed): editor.vue and the M-011 editor surface are untouched by design.
